findings.title: Retry-based deletion is not scoped to unscheduled SMS reminders
findings.body: The second OR branch matches any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method or scheduled state. It can therefore delete EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders and, if an SMS reminder reaches retryCount 2 while also becoming scheduled, delete a reminder already scheduled with Twilio. Deleting the scheduled row removes the referenceId needed to cancel that Twilio message if the booking is cancelled or rescheduled, so the SMS can still be delivered. Scope this branch to method SMS and scheduled: false.

findings.title: Reminders with no recipient or message never accrue retries
findings.body: Scheduling, the retry increment for a null Twilio result, and error handling only occur when both message and sendTo are truthy. A reminder whose booking has no smsReminderNumber/sendTo, or whose generated message is empty, remains scheduled:false with retryCount 0 and is fetched again on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes, which is the retry loop this PR is meant to eliminate. Such permanently unschedulable reminders should increment retryCount or otherwise be logged and eventually removed.

findings.title: Unguarded retry update in catch can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The catch block now awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update without its own error handling. If that update rejects, for example because the row was deleted concurrently, the database is transiently unavailable, or the original exception came from a workflowReminder update, the exception escapes the per-reminder loop and handler. All remaining unscheduled reminders are then skipped for that run and the endpoint errors instead of continuing as the previous log-and-continue behavior did. The increment should be best-effort and not abort processing of subsequent reminders.

findings.title: Retry increments use a stale read instead of an atomic increment
findings.body: Both retry paths set retryCount to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value fetched at the start of the cron run. Overlapping cron invocations, which are possible while this handler sequentially makes slow Twilio calls, can read the same count, both fail, and both write the same incremented value, losing failures and keeping bad reminders alive beyond the intended two failures. Use Prisma's atomic data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } operation instead.

findings.title: No tests cover the new retry and deletion state machine
findings.body: The PR adds retry increments on Twilio-null and exception paths and deletion when retryCount exceeds 1, but adds no automated tests. There is no coverage proving that a failure increments once, a successful schedule does not get deleted, reminders are removed only after the intended number of failures, or one reminder's failure does not prevent later reminders from being processed. Add handler tests with mocked Prisma and Twilio for these cases.
